title: Natural comparison of restricted scalar extension and sheaf tensor
statement: Let (C,J) be a site with C and its morphisms in universe u and the sheafification hypotheses of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Let phi:O -> Oprime be a morphism of commutative ring sheaves. Write U for restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], S=U(Oprime) for the restricted unit module and changeOfRings for the sheafified sectionwise scalar extension [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. There are O-module isomorphisms e_M:U(changeOfRings(phi,M)) -> S tensor_O M for all sheaves of O-modules M. They are natural: for a:M -> N, U(changeOfRingsHom(phi,M,a)) followed by e_N equals e_M followed by id_S tensor a. No flatness assumption is required.

proof.text: Before sheafification, the identity on pure tensors identifies the restricted sectionwise extension Oprime(V) tensor over O(V) M(V) with the presheaf tensor of S and M. Both restrict by restricting each factor, so the identities commute with restrictions. For a module morphism a they both send s tensor m to s tensor a(m). Thus the identifications are natural in M.

Restriction of scalars commutes with module sheafification: both have the same abelian sheafification of the same underlying abelian presheaf. To compare the actions, represent a sheaf section locally by a presheaf section; multiplication by an O-section is on both sides induced by multiplication by its image in Oprime. The locally surjective sheafification unit and separatedness imply equality of these actions. The identity on the associated abelian sheaf therefore gives a module isomorphism. It is natural since the induced maps of abelian sheafifications are the same.

Sheafify the presheaf identifications of step 1 and compose with the restriction/sheafification isomorphisms of step 2. The tensorObjIsoSheafification comparison identifies sheafification of S.val tensor M.val with S tensor M. Its naturality follows from the natural counit of module sheafification and the monoidal tensorator. Compose these natural identifications to obtain e_M and the stated equation. Identity maps on pure tensors also cover zero rings and zero modules.
